newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RESEARCH ALERT - Rules boost red chips - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Rules boost red chips - Salomon.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said on Thursday investor confidence in red chips is expected to be strengthened with the launch of the Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporation Index (HSCCI) and tighter listing rules by China.

"With the HSCCI formally introduced on June 16, we believe there will be a more formal recognition of the importance of the red chip market by institutional investors," Salomon Brothers equity research vice-president Pitzi Lau said in a statement.
"It also provides a benchmark for evaluating the performance and related volatility of leading red-chip stocks," she said.
Red chips are Hong Kong-based companies with Chinese financial backing.
Lau said the listing rules on mainland firms in overseas market signified the official restructuring of China's economy and was expected to cool down the rumours on asset injections.

Under the new addicts, listed companies who seek to spin off assets or increase share capital must first obtain approval from the overseas regulatory authorities and the China Securities Regulatory Commission.
"With the new restrictions on asset injections, investors will focus on fundatmental value for stock picks," Lau said.
She also said difference between the red-chips and H-shares markets was expected to narrow, encouraging investors to focus more on the underlying company and economic fundatmentals.

Under the new scheme, it might be easier to capture China's economic growth through investments in Hong Kong-based companies, such as Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd or New World Infrastructure Ltd, Salomon Brothers said.

However, Lau said some red chips were still attractive. "Investors should select red-chips which have major shareholders with strong political connections in China, solid underlying company fundamentals and sustainable earnings growth," she said.
"With the flight to quality, larger capitalised and well-established companies will continue to be favoured by the market."
